c. Telephone Service
Telephone service is supplied to Harrisburg by the Bell Telephone Company of Pennsylvania. This service is available without limitation to the project area. No exact figures could be obtained as to the extent of use of this service within the project.
d. Public Transportation
Local bus service operating in the urbanized area of Harrisburg is provided by the Harrisburg Railways and Wolf's Bus Lines. In light of the Companies plans to discontinue the service, plans are underway for a take over of the Harrisburg Railways Company (bus operation) by a local area transit authority. Harrisburg Railways is also under contract to provide school bus service to the Harrisburg School District and services the project area.
Two bus routes of the Harrisburg Railways Company provides normal bus service to the project area. Routes running along Second and Green Streets connect the project with the commercial and industrial centers of the City and surrounding areas. Ridership in the project area was observed to be good; however, a survey conducted by an independent consulting firm indicates general dissatisfaction with the present service and a desire by riders for increased services; better routes, special bus lanes, reduced exhaust pollution, shelters and/or benches at bus stops, etc. Obviously; the survey expresses the desires of a percentage of the project residents.
7. Additional Specific Project Descriptions and Information.
The preceeding text of this report, has carried with it a certain amount of detailed information relative to the physical, demographic, economic and social aspects of the actual project area. These discussions were incidental to the topic under discussion and were not intended to be inclusive of all the information necessary for a full and complete understanding of the project area as it now exists. Certain descriptions were complete and they will not be discussed further in Part II.
a. Land Use and Zoning
Reference is made to the general description of project land use patterns given in the discussion of the Project neighborhood (Part II, Paragraph 5 of this report). To better visualize the present land use, an existing Land Use Map is included as appendix F. Note that the project is divided almost equally into two major land uses; residential and commercial/nonresidential. These major patterns are interspersed with various types of other land uses.
